messages:
sara_sales: Heads-up — ACME trial environment started seeing repeated 429s on /v1/embeddings during their bulk ingest earlier today. They run Hosted trial with a 50k token/day budget. Need a short-term mitigation before their demo tomorrow.
---

sara_sales: Customer report: they sent ~500 documents in one job, avg ~200 tokens each. After ~30s into the job they saw 429s and client retrying. Paste of response headers they got below.

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 14:31:16 GMT
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 14
retry-after: 10
x-burst-window-seconds: 1
```

sara_sales: Also got this log snippet from their agent:

```
2026-03-21T14:31:16Z ERROR request_rate_limiter.go:87 rate limit exceeded route=/v1/embeddings acct=acct-123 tokens=102400 reqs_in_min=85
2026-03-21T14:31:17Z WARN  handler.go:214 backoff: 1.2s next_retry
```
---

taylor_support: Thanks — can you confirm the plan (Hosted vs Dedicated) and whether they're on any special trial boost? Also need an ETA for the demo and expected sustained QPS over the window.

sara_sales: Hosted (no Dedicated). Demo tomorrow 10:00 UTC, they want to ingest ~500 documents once, peak ~2.5k tokens/sec for ~3–5 minutes. They're willing to do smaller batches if recommended but prefer one-shot for pipeline simplicity.

max_infra: From the headers and logs it looks like we hit both the per-route req/min cap and the token budget. The x-rate-limit-limit=60 implies 60 reqs/min for that route; 500 docs in one job -> they likely did ~100 requests (5/doc batch) and spiked. Two immediate mitigations:
- Short term: temporary per-route cap bump for acct-123 to 150 reqs/min and increase burst window to allow higher instantaneous concurrency.
- Immediate customer advice: split into smaller batches (<=50 docs) + exponential retry respecting Retry-After.

chandra_eng: Also note tokens: 500 * 200 = ~100k tokens — they exceeded daily token budget (50k). Even if we raise req/min we must raise token quota or they'll hit token enforcement. Recommend a one-time token budget bump to 200k for the trial window.
---

taylor_support: I'll open an internal support request to provision a temporary bump. Creating incident now.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260321-1243 — ratecap/token-bump request for acct-123. Owner: taylor_support. SLA target: 2h.
---

taylor_support: Suggested message/code to send the customer (short):

"We can provision a temporary increase: raise per-route reqs to 150/min and token budget to 200k/day for a 4-hour window. In parallel please split your job into batches of <=50 and implement exponential backoff using Retry-After. We'll monitor.">

Also attaching a quick retry snippet:

```
# pseudocode
for batch in batches:
  resp = post('/v1/embeddings', batch)
  if resp.status == 429:
    wait = int(resp.headers.get('retry-after', 1))
    sleep(backoff.next(wait))
    retry
```

max_infra: I'll schedule the per-route bump tomorrow at 09:50 UTC and enable the short burst window extension. Will keep metrics on the embeddings route and push an alert if error rate > 5%.

chandra_eng: Ops note for whoever approves: change touches hosted rate-limit overrides scoped to acct-123 and route=/v1/embeddings. Make sure the change is ephemeral and auto-reverts after 4h. Also ensure we add a token-budget override + log the usage spike for postmortem.

sara_sales: I'll confirm with ACME that they're ok with splitting into 50-doc batches and accept the temporary token bump. I'll share the revised ingestion plan and demo time. Thanks all, please cc me on the support ticket.

max_infra: cc'ed. If they want permanent higher throughput we should talk Dedicated paths — avoid hitting shared hosted limits.

sara_sales: Understood. I'll update the customer and close loop. :thumbsup:
---

chandra_eng: Small follow-up: customer-side suggestion — add the `prefer-batching` header if they can; we have a helper in the SDK that will pack small items into fewer requests which reduces req/min pressure.

sara_sales: Sending that to them now. Will post customer confirmation when I hear back
